scenes.text: The Pacific Ocean got its name because one explorer saw it on a calm day.
His name was Ferdinand Magellan, and in fifteen nineteen he left Spain with five ships.
He was hunting for a sea route west to the Spice Islands.
Before he found it, one ship was wrecked and another deserted.
On October twenty-first, fifteen twenty, he finally found a narrow passage at the tip of South America.
It took thirty-eight days to fight through that twisting strait.
Then, on November twenty-eighth, three ships sailed out into a huge, quiet ocean.
The water was so calm that he called it pacific, which means peaceful.
But nobody on board knew how big it really was.
They sailed for ninety-nine days before they got fresh food again.
Sick with scurvy, the crew ate rat-fouled biscuits, and finally the leather off the ship's yards.
Today we know the Pacific is the biggest ocean on Earth, with more than half of its free water.
All the continents together could fit inside it.
Magellan never made it home, but one ship reached Spain in fifteen twenty-two, the first to sail around the world.
Would you have signed up for that voyage? Tell me below.

title: Why the Pacific Ocean is called 'peaceful' ⛵
caption: On Nov 28, 1520, Magellan's 3 remaining ships left a brutal strait and found an ocean so calm he called it 'pacific.' Then came 99 days without fresh food.
